gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the FOSSiBOT F2400's solar input stops at 500 W and 50 V (charging cuts off above 48 V, and over-voltage damage is outside warranty), so a second panel wired in series or a high-voltage 400 W panel will not charge it.
standout_why: Compared against cheapestwh.com (cited, opened): it lists only capacity, AC output, chemistry, weight, warranty, price and $/Wh for 12 units of about 2 kWh, with no solar input voltage, wattage, connector, expansion or RV-port data. ChatGPT's own answer gives only capacity, output, chemistry, warranty and weight. The other two rival pages could not be compared: outletpicks.com (cited) and our own dealectric.com page both failed to load (TLS certificate error), so whether they carry solar-input limits is untested, which is why this is 2 and not 3.
decides: It confirms the F2400 as the under-$600 pick for outage or wall-charged use (UPS bypass, car and MC4 cables in the box), but qualifies it for solar: 500 W and 50 V is the ceiling. A shopper who wants fast solar or expansion has no sourced option under $600; the Growatt INFINITY 2000 Pro (1,200 W solar, expandable to 6,144 Wh, TT-30) is $648 on Amazon per cheapestwh.com and $799 at Growatt's store. Price caveat: the F2400 is $669 at FOSSiBOT's own store today; the $599 is the Amazon price as listed by cheapestwh.com, which I did not check on Amazon.

findings.label: Solar input ceiling
findings.note: Manual text: "The input of the solar panel can be up to 500W and the maximum voltage is 50V." The spec table gives the input as 11.5–50 V. Max input current is not stated in the manual. This is a third-party copy of the maker's manual and its spec tables were garbled in extraction; FOSSiBOT's own product page returned HTTP 429 on every attempt.

findings.label: Solar working window and over-voltage behaviour
findings.value: Keep input at 12–48 V; above 48 V over-voltage protection stops charging
findings.note: The manual says nothing about panel open-circuit voltage or series/parallel wiring, so the buyer has to check the panel's Voc against 48 V themselves. No panel Voc was sourced, so no specific panel pairing is claimed.

findings.label: Warranty exclusion stated by maker
findings.value: Damage from exceeding the maximum input voltage is outside warranty
findings.note: Manual text: "If the equipment is damaged by exceeding the maximum voltage, it is outside the scope of warranty." The manual also says free after-sales service isn't guaranteed if the wrong solar panels are connected.

findings.label: Cables in the box
findings.value: AC charging cable, car charging cable (to cigarette lighter), MC4 solar cable, user manual
findings.note: The manual copy names the solar input and both cables as "Anderson" (Anderson-to-MC4, Anderson-to-cigarette-lighter). I could not confirm the connector name on FOSSiBOT's product page, so check it before printing a connector type. The XT60 port (12 V / 25 A) is an output, not a solar input.

findings.label: Solar recharge time at the ceiling
findings.value: About 4 hours with 500 W of panels
findings.note: Maker's claim in the manual, not a measurement. 2,048 Wh / 500 W = 4.1 h at full rated panel output.

findings.label: UPS switchover
findings.note: Store text read through storecheck.py search: "10ms uninterruptible home backup UPS". The manual copy (manualslib.mx) gives about 8 ms and says UPS mode supports only loads under 2,400 W.

findings.label: Port count by region
findings.value: 16 ports on the US version, 13 on the EU version
findings.note: Store text read through storecheck.py search. Matters for grey-import listings: an EU unit is the 220 V, 13-port version.

findings.label: Price at maker's US store
findings.note: storecheck.py search on fossibot.com. This is $69 over the $600 budget; the $599 ChatGPT showed is the Amazon price.
